description: The figure illustrates five schematic bar-chart shapes labeled “Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck,” intended to represent different distributions of values across a small set of categories. In each mini-chart, the categories are arranged along the horizontal axis as a sequence of five adjacent bars with no explicit category tick labels, and there is no visible numeric axis label or tick-marked scale on either axis (the vertical axis is implied by bar height without units or a marked range). In the “Increasing” panel, five gray bars rise from left to right, starting with a very short bar and ending with the tallest bar at the far right. In the “Uniform” panel, all five gray bars appear equal in height. In the “Decreasing” panel, five gray bars descend from left to right, with the tallest bar at the far left and the shortest at the far right. In the “Spindle” panel, the five gray bars form a symmetric profile with shorter bars at both ends and taller bars in the middle (the two central bars appear similarly tall). In the “Bottleneck” panel, the five gray bars show taller bars at both ends with shorter bars in the middle (the central bars appear similar in height), creating a U-shaped profile. There is no legend, no stacking or grouping beyond the five separate panels, and no bars are specially highlighted beyond the consistent gray fill and black outlines; the ordering within each panel follows the left-to-right arrangement implied by the shape name rather than an explicitly labeled sorting rule.
